Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7676); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications:--sabbath (day), week.
BiblicalUsage: The word sábbaton means the Sabbath (that is Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, that is the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications. In 1 Corinthians 16:2, we read, "…lay by him in store, as hath prospered…"; in Acts 1:12, "…unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which…". You hear it again in Colossians 2:16 — "Let no man therefore judge you in meat…" — and in John 5:9, "…bed, and walked: and on the same day…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sábbaton matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. And I believe sábbaton still speaks to us today, because God's word does not go out of date.
